doc: The published version of each bake, read by the bake tools for their
output directory and by the client for the path it requests.
A published bake is immutable: re-baking bumps the version rather than
overwriting objects, which is what invalidates CDN edge and browser
caches. Bumping one here is the whole change.
All three moved together at v6/v6/v4, which is the one time they have:
that is the set baked before a page was named by its quadkey rather than
by a level and a decimal index (pxl-spec bake/quadkey.rs).

$doc: What the published bake declares of itself to the client: `top_level`, the
coarsest level of the pyramid it supplies whole, terrain and POI alike. The
client's floor is leased there, all around the eye, and the far edge is where
that level ends (pxl-kernel world/paging/floor.rs). The dev tile server
answers the same object at the tile root's `source`, with its `--top-level`
(pxl-geo-bake bin/serve_tiles.rs); neither is guessed from what fails.
